sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: Bryum turbinatum is a small moss forming green or pinkish patches up to about 3 cm tall. It grows on damp, sparsely vegetated ground, often sandy or gravelly, including dune slacks and old pits. Its short, swollen capsules narrowed at the mouth are distinctive; sporophytes appear in spring and summer.

sections.title: Image and uses
sections.text: The plate's moss cushion and short, top-shaped capsule match the species. No human food use or other practical use was established. Regional conservation assessments may differ: a local extinction does not imply global extinction.
